title: RLS test coverage ratio
notes: Measured on 2026-09-05 at this promotion's commit: 18/92 = 0.1956521739130435, rounded DOWN to the nearest 0.05 per the task instruction ('first measure it, never 0.90 by default') -> floor 0.15, tolerance 0 (can only rise). itBlockCount from the parser was exactly 92, matching .claude/MEMORY.md's documented '92-case row-level-security (RLS) suite' count, which is strong independent evidence the it()-block extraction is neither over- nor under-counting. Spot-checked by hand: `Message`, `SpokesRecord`, and `Certification` genuinely have ZERO `tx.<model>.`/`prisma.<model>.` references anywhere in src/lib/rls.test.ts despite each having a CREATE POLICY — this is a real, surprising gap (92 policy-bearing tables, only 18 have both a positive and a negative test), not a parser artifact; `Connection`/`Employer`/`EmployerContact`/`JobLead`/`OutboundMessage`/`ConnectionEvent` (the newest, Match & Connect Phase 3/4 additions) plus `Conversation`/`Goal`/`CaseNote`/`Student`/`SageMemory`/`AuditLog`/`CoachingArc`/`StudentAlert`/`StudentWorkProfile`/`Notification`/`NotificationPreference`/`SageOperation` are the 18 covered. Ratio = policy-bearing tables (parsed from every `CREATE POLICY ... ON "visionquest"."<Table>"` across prisma/migrations, deduped) that have at least one POSITIVE and one NEGATIVE case in src/lib/rls.test.ts, over all policy-bearing tables. See scripts/bench/suites/lib/rls-parse.mjs's header comment for the exact positive/negative heuristic (checked against the file: no alternate positive idiom like `.length > 0` or `assert.ok(row)` was found uncaught) and its known limitation (whole-block attribution: a table is 'covered' if ANY of its attributed it() blocks shows positive evidence and ANY shows negative evidence, not necessarily the SAME block — coarser than per-assertion, but explicit and auditable). This is very likely the single most actionable finding in this whole promotion; flagged prominently in the build report for Britt/A0 rather than only left in this file.
